title: High-Level System Design
scope_in: Distributed system design interviews: requirements, estimation, APIs, data models, storage choice, caching, partitioning, replication/consistency, queues/streams, failure modes, observability.
scope_out: Class-level design (prep-lld), implementation code, vendor marketing comparisons.

modes.output: one HLD problem walked through the standard stages, graded vs hidden rubric with one stress probe
rapid trade-off and numbers questions (e.g. quorum maths, when to shard, cache invalidation)
clear a concept: problem, mechanism, trade-offs, when NOT to use it, numbers
re-run weak areas from memory with a harder variant
full interviewer simulation with deep-dive requested on the weakest decision

ladder: URL shortener, pastebin: single DB, simple cache, ID generation.
Rate limiter, notification service, news feed (small), key-value store single node: one scaling idea each.
Twitter timeline, WhatsApp chat, Uber-lite, web crawler: fan-out choices, sharding, queues, hot keys.
Distributed KV store, ticket booking with strong consistency, YouTube, distributed cache: replication, consensus-adjacent trade-offs, failure handling.
Ad click aggregation with exactly-once, global strongly-consistent store, collaborative editor (CRDT/OT), Spanner-like design: deep consistency/time/failure reasoning.

flaws.F-NO-REQUIREMENTS: Jumped to boxes without functional/non-functional requirements.
flaws.F-NO-ESTIMATION: No back-of-envelope numbers where scale decides the design.
flaws.F-ESTIMATION-ERROR: Arithmetic or order-of-magnitude error in estimates.
flaws.F-NO-TRADEOFFS: Chose a component without naming alternatives and costs.
flaws.F-WRONG-STORE: Storage choice inconsistent with access pattern or consistency need.
flaws.F-CONSISTENCY-IGNORED: No stance on consistency/staleness/ordering where it matters.
flaws.F-SPOF: Single point of failure left in the design.
flaws.F-HOTSPOT-IGNORED: Skew / hot key / thundering herd not considered.
flaws.F-NO-FAILURE-MODES: Did not discuss what fails and how it recovers.
flaws.F-BUZZWORD-DROPPING: Named technologies without explaining the mechanism or why.
flaws.F-API-DATA-MISSING: No API or data model before architecture.
flaws.F-DEPTH-LACK: Could not go deep when the interviewer drilled into a component.

x_fields.requirements_missed: Requirements (esp. non-functional) the user never raised.
x_fields.estimation_error_pct: Largest estimation error vs your verified numbers.
x_fields.stress_probe: The probe posed (10x scale, node loss, etc.) and pass/fail.

items_note: prompt, hidden rubric, verified numbers, reference sketch
rubric_body:
Score each 0-2:

| Dimension | Looks for |
|-----------|-----------|
| Requirements | functional + non-functional (latency, availability, consistency, scale), scope cut |
| Estimation | QPS, storage, bandwidth within ~2x of verified numbers, and *used* to decide |
| API & data model | endpoints/entities before boxes |
| Architecture | coherent flow, right components for the load |
| Trade-offs | alternatives named, costs explicit |
| Scalability | partitioning, caching, hotspots, queues where warranted |
| Reliability | failure modes, replication, degradation, SPOFs |
| Depth | convincing deep dive on one component |
outcome_rule: Weighted /16 (Trade-offs, Scalability, Reliability double): **pass** ≥ 70% with no 0 in Requirements or Trade-offs; **partial** 40-70%; **fail** < 40%.
gate_extra: Verify every number (QPS, storage, bandwidth, cache size) with a script; keep the table in the hidden rubric and compare the user's estimates against it, not against intuition.
State consistency/availability claims precisely (e.g. quorum R+W>N reasoning, CAP vs PACELC); if unsure of a protocol detail, say so rather than assert it.
loop_extra:
### Stages (user may reorder; you grade coverage)
Requirements → estimation → API → data model → high-level architecture → deep dive → bottlenecks/failures → stress probe. Do not volunteer the next stage; ask 'what next?' only after silence.
